title: Landfall and Horizon
premise: Freya Reyes, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries for a disaster she may or may not have caused, works the border rivers under a false name. When a flood washes up a chest bearing the seal of Vessia—a nation erased from every map twenty years ago—she finds inside it documents proving the disaster was engineered, and that her missing mother helped build the lie. Hunted by the consortium that erased Vessia and shadowed by a young archivist who wants the truth published, Freya must follow the river upstream to its forbidden source, where the old capital drowned beneath a reservoir. At the source, she must choose between destroying the evidence to stay free and revealing it to clear her name, knowing exposure will cost her everyone who sheltered her. She chooses truth, and in doing so finally stops running.
about_author: Coral Voss is the pen name of a former river expedition leader who spent a decade guiding commercial trips through contested borderlands before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people whose pasts refuse to stay upstream.

chapters.title: The River Keeps What It Takes
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Working a low-season ferry run under an assumed name, Freya guides a nervous client down the Serran River and notes the water running strangely high for the season. When they camp, she admits to herself how long it's been since she stayed anywhere more than a month. Emotional beat: restless competence masking exhaustion.

chapters.title: What the Flood Gave Back
chapters.summary: POV Freya. A flash flood strands her party on a gravel bar, and among the debris Freya spots a brass-bound chest wedged in a willow root. She pries it open alone at night: survey maps of a country called Vessia, sealed orders, and a photograph of her mother standing before a dam that officially never existed. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Two Names, No Country
chapters.summary: POV Freya. In the border town of Kessel's Landing, Freya researches Vessia and finds every reference redacted or burned; a librarian warns her that asking questions here gets people deported. She learns the chest matches others—there were four, and collectors are looking. Emotional beat: the first taste of being hunted rather than hidden.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Wouldn't Leave
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Introduce Tomas Ilic, a junior archivist exiled from the capital for pursuing Vessian records, who has tracked the chest rumors to Kessel's Landing. He confronts Freya clumsily, recognizes her mother in her face, and refuses to be shaken off. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual stubbornness.

chapters.title: Men in Clean Boots
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Consortium agents arrive posing as salvage contractors, offering Freya money for the chest and letting slip they know her real name. She stalls them, realizes her cover is already blown, and slips out of town with Tomas and the chest by night boat. Emotional beat: fear transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Upstream Rules
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya lays out the route: the Serran's headwaters lie in the closed Verrik Reserve above the drowned Vessian capital, passable only before the dry season drops the water levels and closes the gorges. They hire a disreputable boatman, Anselm, who asks no questions for double pay. Emotional beat: the plan crystallizes—the race against the calendar begins.

chapters.title: Anselm's Price
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. The boatman's POV reveals he once ran cargo for Vessian loyalists and lost family when the reservoir filled; he suspects what's in the chest and signs on for reasons he won't name. A consortium patrol boat forces them to abandon the main channel for a treacherous side gorge. Emotional beat: grief disguised as greed.

chapters.title: The Map That Lies Politely
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Deciphering the chest's survey maps, Tomas discovers they're deliberately wrong—drawn to mislead anyone seeking the source—and that corrections are handwritten in his own mentor's notation style, implicating the archive itself. He hides this from Freya. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to war with truth.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckonings
chapters.summary: POV Freya. A brutal rapid run wrecks their supplies and nearly drowns Tomas; Freya saves him but tears open old scars about the mountain disaster, telling him part of the story she's never told anyone. Trust deepens even as she keeps the worst back. Emotional beat: intimacy through shared danger.

chapters.title: The Village Under the Waterline
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Low water exposes the rooftops of a submerged Vessian village; they shelter overnight in a church steeple breaking the surface, where Freya finds fresh offerings left by someone who still remembers. Someone is alive upriver keeping the old country's memory. Emotional beat: awe and homesickness for a home she never had.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Stones
chapters.summary: POV Freya. They meet Maret, an elderly woman who tends memorial cairns along the shore and recognizes the chest instantly—her father carried its twin. Maret tells Freya her mother was the engineer who designed the dam and then tried to stop the flooding of the capital. Emotional beat: the past becoming personal and unbearable.

chapters.title: What My Mother Built
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Reading her mother's letters from the chest, Freya learns the 'mountain disaster' that got her blacklisted was staged to discredit the last witness to the Vessian erasure—her mother. The consortium didn't just erase a country; it erased the people who could prove it. Emotional beat: rage replacing shame.

chapters.title: Tomas's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Consortium agents catch up and offer Tomas full reinstatement and access to the sealed archives if he delivers the chest and abandons Freya. He accepts the meeting, takes the papers, and then burns his own credentials instead, choosing the truth over the institution. Emotional beat: betrayal contemplated, loyalty chosen.

chapters.title: Burned Bridge at Verrik Gate
chapters.summary: POV Freya. The consortium seals the reserve gate ahead of them and puts a price on all three heads; Anselm runs the checkpoint rapids at night in a near-suicidal passage that wrecks the boat beyond repair. They continue on foot with only what they can carry. Emotional beat: no way back now.

chapters.title: Dry Season Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Freya. With five days of water left and three days' climb to the source, Freya calculates margins like the guide she used to be and makes hard cuts—leaving the heavy documents cached with Maret's cairn route, carrying only the core evidence. Emotional beat: discipline as self-preservation and self-erasure at once.

chapters.title: The Hollow Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Climbing into the reserve's karst country, Tomas realizes the 'forbidden source' isn't hidden—it's guarded, because the reservoir's intake tunnels run beneath it, and the consortium maintains a station there to keep the drowned capital undisturbed. He confesses his earlier deception to Freya. Emotional beat: truth between allies, finally.

chapters.title: Station Zero
chapters.summary: POV Freya. They infiltrate the intake station, find records confirming the engineered flood and the staged disaster, and discover her mother's final report—sealed, not destroyed—proving Freya was blacklisted to bury it. Alarms force them to flee deeper into the tunnels toward the source chamber. Emotional beat: vindication arriving hand in hand with capture risk.

chapters.title: Where the River Is Born
chapters.summary: POV Freya. In the vast spring cavern beneath the mountain, cornered by the consortium's director—who offers Freya her life and clean papers in exchange for silence—they fight across the flooded ledges. Anselm sacrifices himself to collapse the intake gate, flooding the station and sealing the evidence's escape route with them. Emotional beat: grief and fury fused into purpose.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya and Tomas ride the released surge out through the spillway, nearly drowning, and surface downstream holding the waterproofed core evidence. The flood has exposed the drowned capital's rooftops for miles—visible now to every village along the river. Emotional beat: survival as testimony; the secret literally surfaces.

chapters.title: Every Village Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Word outruns them: river towns turn out to see the risen city, and Maret's cairns become shrines overnight. Tomas broadcasts copies of the evidence through exile networks while consortium agents close in on the landing where they've gone public. Emotional beat: the truth taking on a life larger than any of them.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Confronting the director one last time before assembled witnesses and foreign observers, Freya surrenders the evidence publicly, accepting arrest and trial rather than another deal—her name cleared in law if not yet in fact. The consortium's local apparatus fractures as its own staff defect with documents. Emotional beat: courage as choosing consequence over flight.

chapters.title: Horizon
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Months later, awaiting the tribunal's ruling, Freya guides a small party up the Serran—not fleeing this time, but leading—to see the exposed capital at dawn. Her blacklist is struck from one country; the other will take longer. She plants her boots on stone that finally belongs somewhere. Emotional beat: stillness earned; the journey ends where identity begins.
